findings.evidence: template/scripts/github_read_cache.py `_page`: `if entry is not None and entry["next"] is not None: command += ["-H", "If-None-Match: ..."]`, with the comment "A last page (no stored next) is always re-read". Single-page resources are PR lists, comment histories of 100 or fewer comments, and every Requirement Issue read. `managed_task.fetch_issue` says "an unchanged issue costs no counted request", which this code makes false. The test `test_warm_read_is_conditional...` asserts `(counted, conditional) == (3, 1)`: one of two pages is still counted. The proposal's motivation (about 140 counted requests per overview) is largely unaddressed.
findings.summary: A stored page with no `rel="next"` link is never revalidated with If-None-Match, so it is always a counted 200. Most cached resources are single-page, so the cache saves almost no counted requests. This conflicts with the design's "Conditional GET per page" and with the spec scenario "only conditional requests that return 304 plus a bounded number of counted requests".

findings.evidence: github_read_cache.py `_store` calls `_load(path)` then `json.dump(data, ...)` of the full file under flock for each page. `_page` and `get_pages` call `cache_path(root)`, which runs `run_git`. Entries are only ever added or replaced, never removed. Under the parallel overview threads this adds lock contention and growing I/O.
findings.summary: The cache has no eviction. Every stored page, including bodies for closed PRs and superseded `?page=N` URLs, stays in one JSON file. Each `_store` reloads, validates and rewrites the whole file, and `cache_path` spawns `git rev-parse` on every page read.
